Diego,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our finance and platform teams are finalizing FY26 budgets this month and asked me to get budgetary numbers for a prepaid/advance-commit arrangement with Redwood. High-level ask below — can you send a compact budgetary quote and a pro forma invoice we can share with procurement?

What we need for planning:
- Two scenarios: 12-month advance prepay and a 24-month advance-commit option.
- For each: list the committed $ value, suggested discount vs list, and an example stepped ramp schedule across quarters (we expect usage to ramp as we pilot features).
- Preferred billing cadence: one invoice up-front if possible, but procurement will flag deferred billing or split invoices if needed.
- Any standard contractual notes on price increases, termination, or credit for unused tokens.

Target for discussion: our leadership is looking at a budget envelope between $800k and $2.5M depending on scope. Please label the attachments as budgetary only.

Appreciate a quick reply — deadline for our budget packet is Oct 15.

Best,
Sofia Ramirez
Head of AI Programs
Bank of Meridian

Sofia — great to hear from you. Attaching a compact budgetary quote (spreadsheet) and a labeled pro forma stub for procurement. Both are budgetary and non-binding. Key summary here so it is easy to paste into your packet: 

Summary (budgetary, list = our standard hosted API pricing):
- 12-month advance prepay (single upfront invoice): Commit $1,100,000 — suggested discount 15% vs list; effective unit cost reduction ~18% after batching and KV cache adjustments. Proposed ramp (consumption % of commit): Q1 30%, Q2 50%, Q3 75%, Q4 100%.
- 24-month advance-commit (single upfront invoice, multi-year term price): Commit $2,200,000 — suggested discount 22% vs list; effective unit cost reduction ~25% with recommended quantization profile. Proposed ramp: Year 1 Q1 20%, Q1 Q2 combined 40%, end of Year 1 65%, Year 2 reach 100% by Q3.

Billing & terms (budgetary suggestion):
- Standard: invoice upfront, net 30.
- If procurement needs split-invoicing: we can split into 2 invoices (50/50) with same effective discount; legal needs to confirm.
- Price protection: fixed unit rates for the term; model upgrades to compatible variants included; material model changes subject to review.
- Unused commit: standard yearly true-up — credits can be applied to next 90 days of usage or refunded pro rata for multi-year with approval.

Attachments included: 20251002-BoM-FY26-Advance-Commit-Quote.xlsx (budget worksheet), and a one-page labeled pro forma.

Next steps: if the 24-month looks promising, can I loop in Karthik (sales) and Evelyn (finance) for internal approval and a formal pro forma for procurement?

Thanks — I will hold for your direction.

Diego Fernandez

Diego — I like the structure. A few notes from quota and commercial: 
- Authorize AE-level binding offer up to 15% discount for 12mo. For 24mo, AE can offer up to 20% with Finance sign-off; anything above 20% requires VP approval.
- Given the strategic nature of the account, propose conditional uplift to 22% for 24mo if Bank of Meridian commits to a 20% year-over-year usage growth clause in the SOW. This protects unit economics.
- Add a rollback clause: if actual usage at calendar quarter checkpoints is below 60% of the committed ramp for two consecutive quarters, we reserve the right to revisit pricing.

If legal and finance are comfortable with the wording, this will give us a clean path to present a 22% figure tied to commercial milestones.

Karthik
VP, Sales Operations
